about: Trees found while researching Lisbon that are not published. 'leads' failed only on our evidence bar, on the count, or on being folded into a shipped entry; they are the raw material if Lisbon grows. 'blocked' must never ship, each with its one-line reason. Register figures are ICNF's: girth and height in METRES, and age_register is the age at last_measured, not today.

leads.source: ICNF, Arvoredo de Interesse Publico (CC BY 4.0)
leads.note: Researched this pass: no independent second source found for this specific tree despite searching; 'Bairro do Restelo' in the register lugar field is a neighbourhood name, not a precise public site, so the exact spot (park, street or private garden) is still unconfirmed. Needs a sharper address before it can ship.

leads.note: Jardim 9 de Abril flame tree. Register species is only 'Brachychiton spp.', so the species is unresolved and no canonical common name can be set; it would break the one-name-per-species build check. Third tree of the Jardim 9 de Abril walk, worth resolving.

leads.classified: Aviso n.º 14/2012 de 13 julho de 2012, Autoridade Florestal Nacional
leads.source: ICNF, Arvoredo de Interesse Publico (CC BY 4.0)
leads.note: Researched this pass: the Observatorio Astronomico de Lisboa at Tapada da Ajuda is now part of the Museu Nacional de Historia Natural e da Ciencia with guided visits only on Wednesdays, not open walk-up access. Also registered as a 'Conjunto arboreo' of 4 dragon trees, so it needs a collectibility judgement (one obvious place to stand, or not) as well as an access resolution before it could ship.

leads.source: ICNF, Arvoredo de Interesse Publico (CC BY 4.0)
leads.note: PIN CONFLICT with published lis_005. Register lugar is 'Praca de S.Bento', our published tipuana is 'Jardim de Sao Bento', and the two points are 244 m apart. Either two separate classified tipuanas or one tree with one wrong coordinate. Resolve before either pin is called confirmed.

leads.source: ICNF, Arvoredo de Interesse Publico (CC BY 4.0)
leads.note: Moreton Bay Fig, Rua de Marvila. Register girth 12.2 m and age 200 at 2010, by far the largest girth of any Lisbon fig in the register. Sits alone in Marvila, 1.8 km from the nearest published tree, so it thickens no walk today. Access and vitality both unchecked.

leads.place: Terreno anexo ao Palácio da Luz
leads.source: ICNF, Arvoredo de Interesse Publico (CC BY 4.0)
leads.note: Researched this pass: the register's 'Terreno anexo ao Palacio da Luz' sits beside the Seminario da Luz, owned by the Franciscan Order since 1939 (a private religious property); one planning document mentions a future public green area west of the palace but gives no evidence it exists yet or covers this tree. Access unconfirmed either way; do not ship without an on-the-ground check.
